title: Never Give Up
intro: Never Give Up asks for quiet before it asks for endurance. The questions distinguish recognising a cruel situation from accepting it as the final shape of one's life. Perseverance then rests on a limited bodily fact: there is still some strength left. Unlike 'All In', the song does not make a particular rank or level of success the condition for stopping. Its encouragement is smaller and more credible because it acknowledges depletion rather than pretending that determination creates an inexhaustible person.
reading: Quiet enables self-address; acknowledging conditions need not mean surrender; endurance is grounded in remaining capacity.

revisions.t51-n1: The repeated verb asks for a little settling or quiet, not necessarily permanent isolation. That modest request matters before the title's large imperative. The person needs enough space from other people's words to hear and answer their own situation. Rest and continuation are not treated as automatic opposites: a boundary around attention can be part of what makes further action possible.
revisions.t51-n2: The lyric first demands that the listener believe reality is cruel, then challenges the conclusion that they must accept their allotted fate. Recognition and resignation are different acts. This also reopens the ending of 'Life Life Life', where fate had to be accepted. The album can contain both formulas because they are positions voiced under different pressures, rather than chapters in one consistently stated doctrine.
revisions.editorial-51-still-strength: The grand instruction to persist comes back to what remains in a body. 'At least' and 'still' make the claim finite: this is not a promise that effort will always be available or automatically rewarded. The ending finds something usable now. That scale gives the encouragement its force without turning the exhausted person into a failure for needing the quiet requested at the beginning.
